question: Why is a tiered facility structure important for rural healthcare delivery?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any secondary or tertiary hospitals
options.B: It forces all patients to travel to cities for basic checkups
options.C: It ensures patients receive care at the simplest appropriate level first
options.D: It prevents community health workers from seeing pregnant women

explanation: Stepped structures prevent higher-level facilities from getting overcrowded with minor health issues that local posts can easily handle. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which blood test is mainly used to screen pregnant women for an active Hepatitis B infection?

options.A: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)
options.B: Hepatitis B surface antibody (Anti-HBs)
options.C: Total Hepatitis B core antibody (Anti-HBc)
options.D: Hepatitis B e antibody (Anti-HBe)

explanation: Finding HBsAg in the blood shows that the person currently has the Hepatitis B virus. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T7#BMP221_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why is it important for a midwife to note how a patient's temperature was measured?

options.A: Different body sites give slightly different baseline temperature readings.
options.B: Armpit readings are always higher than internal core values.
options.C: The brain only responds to temperatures taken in the ear.
options.D: Only oral thermometers can detect hypothermia.

explanation: Sites like the mouth, ear, and armpit measure temperature a little differently, so clinicians account for these variations during assessment. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T5#BMP111_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge in Nigerian tertiary health facilities?

options.A: Frequent electricity grid failures and heavy reliance on generators
options.B: Breakdown of advanced diagnostic machines with delayed repairs
options.C: High reliance on out-of-pocket payments by struggling patients
options.D: Excessive availability of surplus specialist staff in all departments

explanation: Tertiary facilities face severe staff shortages rather than a surplus of specialist personnel. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the main difference between skeletal traction and skin traction?

options.A: Skeletal traction uses foam boots placed over the foot
options.B: Skeletal traction uses pins inserted directly into the bone
options.C: Skeletal traction requires much lighter weights than skin
options.D: Skeletal traction is only used for upper arm fractures

explanation: Skeletal traction relies on surgical pins or wires placed straight into bone tissue, allowing heavier weights for deep alignment. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T3#BMP216_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary function of professional associations such as the National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives?

options.A: To build private commercial hospitals across the country
options.B: To set legal penalties for criminal offenses in courts
options.C: To advocate for worker welfare and uphold professional ethics
options.D: To import pharmaceutical drugs from overseas manufacturers

explanation: Professional associations exist to protect the interests of their members, promote high ethical standards, and support professional growth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a major component included in a comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation program for COPD patients?

options.A: Intravenous antibiotic administration
options.B: Supervised physical exercise training
options.C: Mandatory prolonged bed rest routines
options.D: Surgical removal of damaged alveoli

explanation: Pulmonary rehabilitation uses safe, guided exercise to build body strength and endurance, which helps patients feel less breathless during daily activities. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T9#BMP125_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is a common post-operative symptom that midwives should expect after a cervical stitch procedure?

options.A: Severe continuous contractions
options.B: Mild cramping or backache
options.C: Heavy blood clots in the urine
options.D: High fever with chills

explanation: Manipulating the cervix during the stitching process frequently causes mild, temporary cramping or lower back discomfort. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h4)

question: What physical sign helps a midwife tell a simple hydrocele apart from other scrotal swellings?

options.A: It transilluminates brightly when a light source is applied
options.B: It causes severe acute pain in the neonate
options.C: It feels hard and bony upon palpation
options.D: It disappears completely when the infant cries

explanation: Because a hydrocele is filled with clear fluid, light passes through it easily, lighting up the scrotum during transillumination. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which medication class is the main first treatment to calm immune-related kidney damage?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Antifungals
options.C: Anticoagulants
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Corticosteroids like prednisone are used to calm down immune activity in the kidneys and stop protein loss. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h5)

question: What main issue usually triggers acute appendicitis?

options.A: Infection from heavy parasite loads
options.B: Obstruction of the appendiceal lumen
options.C: Direct blunt trauma to the abdomen
options.D: Chronic twisting of the mesentery

explanation: Blockage of the narrow tube starts a chain reaction of mucus buildup, pressure, and reduced blood flow to the tissue. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T6#BMP125_U3_T6_h1)

question: How do prostaglandins help oxytocin during delivery?

options.A: By cooling down the temperature of the pelvis
options.B: By stopping blood flow to the lower uterine segment
options.C: By neutralizing oxytocin to prevent over-contraction
options.D: By making the uterine muscle cells more sensitive to contractions

explanation: Prostaglandins prepare the uterine muscle so that oxytocin can trigger stronger and more coordinated contractions. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference between passive and active cellular transport?

options.A: Active transport requires energy while passive transport does not
options.B: Passive transport requires energy while active transport does not
options.C: Passive transport only happens in dead cells
options.D: Active transport only moves water molecules

explanation: Active transport uses cellular energy like ATP to move substances, whereas passive transport relies on natural molecular motion without using energy. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T3#BMP111_U1_T3_h1)

question: A woman arrives at the labour ward with a neglected transverse lie and ruptured membranes. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Prepare for an emergency caesarean section without delay
options.B: Encourage maternal pushing to deliver the shoulder vaginally
options.C: Administer oxytocin infusion to speed up the uterine contractions
options.D: Attempt external cephalic version on the labour couch

explanation: An operative delivery via caesarean section is the only safe method to resolve an active transverse lie in labour. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T6#BMP311_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which preparation is vital to manage potential shock during an MROP?

options.A: Placing a heavy sandbag directly on the patient's chest
options.B: Turning off all lights in the labor ward to calm the patient
options.C: Giving the patient a heavy meal to keep her energy high
options.D: Securing a large-bore intravenous line for fluids and drugs

explanation: Retained placental tissue combined with open blood vessels carries a high risk of shock, so having an IV line ready is essential. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is anonymous grading helpful when scoring essay papers?

options.A: It guarantees that every student will pass
options.B: It makes tallying total scores much faster
options.C: It stops lecturer bias based on a student's past reputation
options.D: It removes the need for a marking guide

explanation: Hiding names stops personal impressions from swaying how a marker grades an open-ended essay. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why is public health education regarding open fractures and traditional bone-setters crucial in Nigeria?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any surgical intervention in the country
options.B: To ensure traditional bonesetters receive government medical licenses
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of importing hospital equipment
options.D: To reduce delays in medical care and prevent severe bone infections

explanation: Community education helps people recognize the risks of unsterile manipulation and encourages prompt hospital care for trauma. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T4#BMP216_U3_T4_h8)

question: What color tag is assigned to patients needing immediate life-saving treatment during triage?

options.A: Green
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Black
options.D: Red

explanation: A red tag indicates critical, life-threatening injuries that require immediate intervention to save the person's life. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T8#BMP110_U7_T8_h6)

question: Name the heat exchange process that involves liquid changing into a gas on the skin surface.

options.A: Conduction
options.B: Evaporation
options.C: Radiation
options.D: Convection

explanation: Evaporation removes heat as moisture turns from liquid to vapor on the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T12#BMP111_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why is involving a trusted family member or partner in care planning so important?

options.A: They prevent the midwife from having to talk to the patient
options.B: They replace the need for professional psychiatric medication entirely
options.C: They can help spot early warning signs of an oncoming mood relapse
options.D: They are legally required to take over all clinical decision-making

explanation: Family members living closely with the patient often notice subtle behavioral changes before an episode fully develops. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why does a midwife check newborn reflexes and muscle tone during the first physical exam?

options.A: To measure the baby's total blood volume
options.B: To prevent congenital heart defects
options.C: To determine the infant's future intelligence
options.D: To check for signs of nervous system depression or birth trauma

explanation: Normal reflexes and muscle tone show that the newborn's nervous system is healthy and working properly after birth. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T1#BMP121_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the most frequent complication that happens during a hemodialysis treatment session?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Liver failure
options.C: Hypotension
options.D: Severe jaundice

explanation: Rapid removal of fluid from the vascular space frequently leads to low blood pressure during treatment sessions. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T8#BMP216_U1_T8_h5)

question: How can a nurse best safeguard autonomy for an involuntary psychiatric patient?

options.A: By avoiding any form of medication administration to prevent infringing on freedom
options.B: By granting the patient unconditional permission to leave the ward whenever they choose
options.C: By allowing family members to make all clinical decisions without consulting the patient
options.D: By involving the patient in care decisions as much as their current mental state allows

explanation: Autonomy is respected by encouraging participation and choice wherever possible, even within the bounds of involuntary care. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T4#BMP223_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary role of Langerhans cells in the epidermis?

options.A: Secreting oily sebum to maintain skin moisture
options.B: Generating thick layers of protective keratin protein
options.C: Acting as immune sentinels to capture foreign antigens
options.D: Producing the dark pigment known as melanin

explanation: Langerhans cells detect and capture invading germs or foreign particles in the skin and take them to lymph nodes. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T4#BMP111_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why does following an incorrect software dosage prompt still hold the clinician liable?

options.A: Midwives must always use independent clinical judgment to verify care
options.B: Electronic systems are incapable of making calculation errors
options.C: Hospitals never purchase software tested by clinical experts
options.D: Software vendors have complete legal immunity in all healthcare settings

explanation: Clinicians cannot shift total blame to a machine because professional responsibility requires checking computer outputs against patient needs. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T4#BMP123_U5_T4_h6)

question: How does the fetus get enough magnesium if the mother's dietary intake is low?

options.A: The fetus absorbs magnesium through the mother's skin
options.B: The fetus makes its own magnesium inside the amniotic sac
options.C: The placenta actively transports available magnesium across to the fetus
options.D: The placenta blocks all magnesium to protect the mother

explanation: The placenta prioritizes getting minerals to the fetus even when maternal reserves are low. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T8#BMP118_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which dermal receptors are primarily responsible for detecting deep pressure?

options.A: Meissner corpuscles
options.B: Epidermal melanocytes
options.C: Pacinian corpuscles
options.D: Free nerve endings

explanation: Pacinian corpuscles are specialized mechanoreceptors located deeper in the dermis that respond strongly to heavy pressure and vibration. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T2#BMP111_U4_T2_h6)

question: What happens when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back for too long without a hip tilt?

options.A: Leg blood flow increases and causes cramps
options.B: The baby stops moving completely
options.C: The heavy uterus presses on major blood vessels and lowers blood pressure
options.D: Her breathing becomes very deep and easy

explanation: Pressure on the main blood vessels reduces blood return to the heart, making the mother dizzy and lowering blood flow to the baby. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do patients receiving adrenergic medications often feel anxious or shaky?

options.A: The drugs stimulate the central nervous system much like a stress response.
options.B: The drugs directly destroy red blood cells carrying oxygen to the brain.
options.C: The drugs cause a sudden drop in core body temperature.
options.D: The drugs block all electrical activity in peripheral nerves.

explanation: By mimicking fight-or-flight hormones, these medications naturally cause feelings of jitteriness, tremors, and anxiety. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T2#BMP124_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing according to Orem's foundational philosophy?

options.A: Prescribing medication for acute physical conditions
options.B: Replacing the family entirely during hospital stays
options.C: Helping individuals meet their own health needs
options.D: Taking complete control of all daily life activities

explanation: Orem viewed nursing as specialized help directed at enabling patients to regain or maintain their personal self-care abilities. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is true about non-probability sampling when choosing who to study?

options.A: A computer selects names purely by random chance
options.B: Every person in the population must be listed
options.C: Sample sizes must always exceed one thousand
options.D: Not every member has an equal chance of selection

explanation: Non-probability sampling means participants are chosen deliberately rather than by random chance, so not everyone has an equal opportunity to be picked. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does having too much cortisol lead to high blood sugar?

options.A: By forcing the kidneys to reabsorb all filtered blood glucose
options.B: By destroying insulin stored inside the pancreatic beta cells
options.C: By accelerating the rapid digestion of dietary carbohydrates
options.D: By stimulating gluconeogenesis and causing insulin resistance

explanation: Cortisol encourages the liver to make more glucose and stops body cells from responding properly to insulin, leading to high blood sugar. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T8#BMP216_U2_T8_h3)

question: A midwife checks the patient's current stability and ward environment before passing a duty to a junior nurse. Which Right is being applied?

options.A: Right task
options.B: Right person
options.C: Right direction
options.D: Right circumstance

explanation: Evaluating the patient's current condition and the ward setting falls directly under the Right circumstance principle. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a major challenge faced by modern midwives working in various parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Having too many doctors and no patients to care for
options.B: Bridging global standards with local infrastructural gaps
options.C: The complete absence of pregnant women in rural areas
options.D: An absolute surplus of high-tech maternity hospitals

explanation: Midwives must strive to deliver high-quality global care standards even when working in facilities that may lack basic equipment or steady power. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of using proper body mechanics during nursing duties?

options.A: To reduce the cost of hospital equipment
options.B: To protect the nurse's spine from strain
options.C: To speed up the time spent on ward rounds
options.D: To make patient rooms look neat and orderly

question: Why is acute liver failure considered a medical emergency?

options.A: It always results from severe bacterial infections of the bloodstream
options.B: It can only be treated with major abdominal surgery in tertiary hospitals
options.C: It destroys healthy liver tissue rapidly without prior warning signs
options.D: It causes immediate and permanent kidney damage in every patient

question: A mother has just boiled her kettle for formula preparation. What should she do next for safe mixing?

options.A: Let the water cool for a short time so it stays above 70°C before mixing
options.B: Mix the powder immediately while the water is still boiling vigorously
options.C: Wait until the water becomes completely cold before adding the powder
options.D: Store the boiling water in a flask until the next feeding time

explanation: Water must be allowed to cool slightly but remain hot enough (at least 70°C) to kill bacteria in the powder without scalding equipment or destroying all nutrients. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T8#BMP214_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which finding on a routine urine dipstick is a classic warning sign for pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Bilirubin
options.B: Protein
options.C: Ascorbic acid
options.D: Urobilinogen

explanation: Finding significant protein in the urine of a pregnant woman is a key indicator used to diagnose pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T1#BMP216_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three core pillars of a true experimental design?

options.A: Control
options.B: Retrospection
options.C: Manipulation
options.D: Randomization

question: Which monitoring method uses heat-resistant bacterial spores to check that an autoclave is working correctly?

options.A: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.B: Chemical indicator tape
options.C: Visual inspection of shine

question: Where does sperm production actually take place inside the testes?

options.A: Epididymal head
options.B: Scrotal skin folds

question: Which type of medication is usually given for quick relief during a severe Crohn's disease flare?

options.A: Antacids and proton pump inhibitors
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Bulk-forming laxatives

question: What term is commonly used for someone receiving preventive care in the community?

options.A: Casualty
options.B: Patient
options.C: Client
options.D: Inmate

question: Why is plotting a newborn's weight on a growth chart important?

options.A: It helps anticipate specific risks like low blood sugar or macrosomia.

options.C: It replaces the need to perform a complete physical head-to-toe examination.
options.D: It determines the exact date when the baby will be discharged from the ward.

explanation: Knowing the growth percentile helps midwives watch out for potential blood sugar or growth-related issues. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T2#BMP214_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is good leadership especially important in healthcare settings with limited resources?

options.A: It ensures the optimal use of limited available drugs and personnel
options.B: It automatically prevents all medical errors in the maternity unit
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for government healthcare funding
options.D: It allows midwives to avoid doing direct clinical shift work

explanation: When resources like staff and supplies are scarce, strong leadership helps maximize their utility to keep patients safe. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T1#BMP312_U1_T1_h1)

question: What practice causes most accidental needlestick injuries among maternity staff and must be completely avoided?

options.A: Carrying a safety box with one hand down the corridor
options.B: Recapping used injection needles or suture needles
options.C: Placing suture scissors on a sterile instrument tray
options.D: Washing metal speculums in a cold decontamination basin

question: Why is visual observation of a procedure critical for midwifery students before trying it themselves?

options.A: It shows correct physical handling, equipment use, and safety steps.
options.B: It eliminates the need for supervised practice sessions.
options.C: It proves clinical documentation expertise.
options.D: It guarantees zero mistakes during real emergency births.

explanation: Watching a skilled performance gives learners a mental model of correct technique and safety measures before their own hands-on attempt. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective data gathered during an antenatal assessment?

options.A: A feeling of anxiety about upcoming labor

question: What is the standard way that most bacteria reproduce asexually?

options.B: Binary fission
options.C: Meiotic division

question: Why are newborns especially sensitive to anti-anxiety drugs taken near the end of pregnancy?

options.A: Fetal blood binds too tightly to the drugs

options.C: Their immature livers and kidneys process drugs slowly

question: What is the biggest social barrier for pregnant women seeking help for substance use?

options.A: Complete absence of any physiological withdrawal signs
options.B: Mandatory government fees for addiction counseling
options.C: A total lack of interest in attending antenatal clinics
options.D: Severe fear of social stigma and child custody loss

question: Why is it helpful to brief the student before meeting the patient at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any questions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any supervision by the instructor
options.C: It gives the learner time to review relevant clinical knowledge and focus
options.D: It ensures the student can perform the delivery completely alone

explanation: Knowing the focus beforehand helps students pay attention to the right clinical signs during the session. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why are normal sodium levels so important for brain function?

options.A: Sodium acts as the primary energy source for brain cell mitochondria

options.C: Sodium molecules form the structural scaffolding of neurons

question: A woman with a rhesus-negative blood type gives birth to a rhesus-positive baby in a clinic. What is the best action?

options.A: Give the newborn a live polio vaccine immediately to stimulate active immunity
options.B: Schedule the mother for routine tetanus toxoid booster injections next week

question: What molecule serves as the main energy currency for bacterial cells?

options.A: Ribosomal ribonucleic acid
options.B: Adenosine triphosphate
options.C: Deoxyribonucleic acid
options.D: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide

question: What is the main problem with using unclear instructions at an OSCE station door?

options.A: It makes the examination take twice as long
options.B: It prevents the use of standardized patients
options.C: It causes student panic and unfair grading

question: Why do clinicians check serum creatinine levels when kidney issues are suspected?

options.C: It measures the exact amount of sugar stored in the bladder

question: What is a primary type of talk therapy used to treat OCD?

question: What does passing the bloody show mean in late pregnancy?

options.C: The amniotic fluid is fully infected

question: What is the primary infection-control reason for keeping hospital patients' nails clean and trimmed?

options.A: To make it easier to apply topical antiseptic creams
options.B: To prevent the nails from breaking off into the bedsheets
options.C: To stop the patient from biting their own fingers

question: Why is drying a newborn baby thoroughly right after birth so important?

options.C: It removes vernix caseosa to prevent skin infections

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of poorly controlled gestational diabetes?

question: How does glucose mainly cross the placenta to reach the baby?

question: Why is it important to document specific nail abnormalities like localized redness and swelling in the clinical chart?
